# Broadcastify feed-owner fixtures: samples and **guesses**, all invented

Nothing in this directory came from Broadcastify. Every feed id, mount, county, listener
count and timestamp is made up; the files only reproduce the *shapes* that keyup has to
read, so the tests can say what each parser expects without shipping anyone's feed data
or a copy of a third-party page.

## Samples of an observed shape

These four mirror responses that were seen once while the parsers were written. The
shape is what matters, and each test asserts it field by field; the values are invented.

- `feed_sample.json` is an `a=feed&type=json` response. The envelope is a capital `Feed`
  holding a *list*, the count is plainly `listeners`, "up" is `status: 1`, and the
  response carries **no history at all**: one instant, no series, nothing to backfill.
- `archives_day_sample.json` is a per-day archive listing in the clock-range form
  (`{"archive": "10:35 PM - 10:50 PM", "url": …}`), with one block that crosses midnight.
- `feed_page_sample.html` is a stand-in for the *public* feed page, reduced to the markup
  `app/bcfy_stats/public_page.py` reads: the detail table (status badge, `data-since`,
  listener count) and the 24-hour sparkline, one `<rect class="listen-sparkline-bar">`
  per hour with its count in a `<title>`, plus the Min / Max / Now summary. That markup
  is undocumented on Broadcastify's side and can change on any deploy, which is why the
  parser is total and this file exists to record what it looked like.
- `owner_hourly_sample.csv` and `owner_uptime_sample.csv` are the two CSVs the feed-owner
  dashboard offers (Manage → the feed → Statistics), regenerated by `../gen_fixtures.py`.
  They keep the structural quirks the importer tests assert by value: newest row first;
  179 rows each; an outage that sits in two adjacent hourly rows (`2026-09-04 04:00`
  short by five of fifteen checks, `03:00` by exactly one), which is what shows the
  timestamps are **UTC**; and three incident days (412 listeners on 2026-05-17, 171 on
  06-03, 118 on 07-11) far above every ordinary day, so a clamp or an outlier filter in
  the parser would show up as a failure.

## Guesses

Every other file is a **plausible invention**. Broadcastify documents the *parameters*
(`a`, `type`, `feedId`, `u`, `p`) and not the response body, and one account's answer is
not a schema, so the guesses stay: they prove the client copes with several plausible
shapes (camelCase and snake_case, a bare object and a wrapped one, JSON and XML,
booleans as `1`/`true`/`"online"`) and that whatever it fails to recognize is still stored
verbatim in `bcfy_feed_samples.raw`. The `archives_*` guesses are the same kind of thing
for the day list and the per-day listing.

When a new response shape turns up (`keyup bcfy-stats probe`, or
`POST /api/admin/bcfy-stats/probe`), add its field names to `FIELD_ALIASES`, add an
invented sample of the shape here, and drop whichever guess it contradicts. Do not commit
a captured response as it arrived. See `docs/BCFY_STATS.md`.
